messages.content:
Work out the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Think in three steps: first name the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, second name the ICD-10-AM chapter letter it belongs to, third give the three-character category.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: Irreversible airflow limitation in a heavy smoker with an infective exacerbation is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chapter J, category J44.
CODE: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: ST elevation with a rising troponin and culprit-vessel stenting is an acute myocardial infarction, chapter I, category I21.
CODE: I21

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary

Patient Name: [REDACTED]
Patient Age: 45 years
Gender: Male
Date of admission: [REDACTED]
Date of discharge: [REDACTED]
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted with symptoms of intermittent fever, chills and rigors along with night sweats, loss of appetite, and weight loss. The patient also had a transient macular rash and generalized painful lymphadenopathy. Synovitis involving lower limb small joints was noted following the presentation that progressed to larger joints in the lower and upper limbs. Laboratory investigations revealed high white cell counts, normocytic anemia and high inflammatory markers which were in a rising trend following the onset of arthritis. The patient was diagnosed as a case of DLBCL following a lymph node biopsy.

Treatment:
The patient was started on non-steroidal anti-inflammatory agents and colchicine for the arthritis but there was no response to treatment. Treatment with RCHOP chemotherapy commenced which showed a marked response in the synovitis following the first cycle of therapy. The patient completed the chemotherapy with intermittent infections.

Summary:
The patient presented with symptoms of intermittent fever, chills, and rigors along with night sweats, loss of appetite, and weight loss. The patient had synovitis involving the small and large joints of the upper and lower limbs with a lower limb predominance. Laboratory investigations revealed high white cell counts and anemia. A lymph node biopsy was positive for DLBCL. The patient underwent RCHOP chemotherapy which resulted in the complete resolution of synovitis. The patient was discharged in stable condition with a follow-up plan for further evaluation and management.

Write your reasoning in at most three short sentences, then a final line of exactly 'CODE: <letter><digit><digit>'.

text:
Constitutional symptoms, lymphadenopathy and a paraneoplastic polyarthritis are explained by diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, confirmed on lymph node biopsy and treated with R-CHOP. This is a neoplasm, chapter C. The category is C83 (non-follicular lymphoma, diffuse large B-cell lymphoma C83.3).

CODE: C83
